### Let's Refresh Our Memories: What is Research?

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("compass", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**A Journey of Discovery**

Research is a systematic investigation to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Question-Driven**

Every great discovery begins with a well-framed question that guides your direction.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Evidence-Based**

Research relies on gathering and analyzing evidence rather than opinions or assumptions.
]
]

---
### Refresher cont'd: Core Principles of Good Research

#### <span style="color:#0148A4;">No matter what the field is</span>

### Refresher cont'd: Principle 1 &mdash; Be Curious

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**The Starting Point: Curiosity**
]

.content-box-blue[.font90[
**Wonder** &mdash; Asking questions such as

"Why?" &nbsp;&nbsp; "When?" &nbsp;&nbsp; "How much?"<br>
"What if?" &nbsp;&nbsp; "How come?" &nbsp;&nbsp; "For whom?"<br>
"Under what circumstances?"<br>
"What is the trend?"<br>
"What is the relationship between?"

drives meaningful research.
]]
]

### Refresher cont'd: The Research Process

.font110[The journey from question to insight follows these essential steps:]

.font80[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>1. Ask a Question</strong><br>
    Formulate a clear, specific question worth investigating.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>2. Gather Information</strong><br>
    Review the literature & collect relevant data through appropriate methods.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>3. Analyze the Information</strong><br>
    Examine data for patterns, trends, and meaning.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>4. Draw Conclusions</strong><br>
    Develop evidence-based answers to your original question.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("share-nodes", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>5. Share Findings</strong><br>
    Communicate results effectively to appropriate audiences.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

--

.center[.font120[<strong style="color:#0148A4;">Today we focus on Step 1: Asking a Good Question!</strong>]]

### Your Research Question is a Compass

.pull-left[
```{r img4, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/04-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("compass", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; A well-framed question acts as your compass, pointing you toward useful answers.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("rotate", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Vague questions lead to circular research. Specific questions drive you to meaningful discoveries.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("triangle-exclamation", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Without the right question, even the best research efforts might not yield satisfying answers.
]

### Case Study: The Library Problem

.pull-left[.font80[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Initial Question</strong><br>
  "How can we make teens read more books?"</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Reframed Question</strong><br>
  "What are the barriers to teens' library use?"</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Research Method</strong><br>
  Surveyed classmates about library usage.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">4</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Discovery</strong><br>
  Limited Wi-Fi and few comfortable spaces deterred teens.</div>
</div>
]]

### Case Study: Solar Panel Investigation

<br>

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Initial Question**

"How can we improve solar panel efficiency?"
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Better Question**

"What factors are limiting our school's solar panel performance?"
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Findings**

Shade, incorrect tilt, and dust accumulation were the issues.
]

### What Makes a Good Research Question? BRIC-FOR

.pull-left[
```{r img6, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/06-img.png")

```

.pull-right[

<br>

### <strong style="color:#A4123F;">B</strong>alanced (Well-Scoped)
### <strong style="color:#A4123F;">R</strong>elevant & <strong style="color:#A4123F;">I</strong>nteresting
### <strong style="color:#A4123F;">C</strong>lear & <strong style="color:#A4123F;">F</strong>ocused
### <strong style="color:#A4123F;">O</strong>pen-ended
### <strong style="color:#A4123F;">R</strong>esearchable
]

---
### .font70[.red[B]RIC-FOR:] Balanced in Scope (aka Well-Scoped Questions)

.three-col[
.col[
.content-box-yellow[
**Too Broad**

"What is the history of the United States?"

Spans hundreds of years and countless topics.
]
]
.col[
.content-box-yellow[
**Too Narrow**

"What was the price of bread in our town on January 1, 1950?"

More of a trivia fact than a research project.
]
]
.col[
.content-box-green[
**Just Right**

"How have food prices in our town changed from 1950 to today, and why?"

Focused yet allows for meaningful analysis.
]
]
]

---
### .font70[B.red[RI]C-FOR:] Relevant and Interesting Questions

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("heart", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Personal Relevance**

Choose topics that matter to you&mdash;you'll stay more engaged.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("people-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Community Impact**

Research that addresses local issues can have real-world applications.
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Example**

"How does sleep affect test scores among students in my grade?"
]
]

.pull-right[
```{r img7, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="72%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/07-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

---
### .font70[BRI.red[C-F]OR:] Clear and Focused Questions

<br>

.pull-left[
.content-box-yellow[
**Too Broad**

"What causes climate change?"

This spans science, policy, history, and economics&mdash;a lifetime of work!
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
**Well-Focused**

"How do car emissions contribute to climate change in my city?"

Narrows to one cause, one effect, and one location.
]
]

---
### .font70[BRIC-F.red[O]R:] Open-Ended Questions

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-yellow[
**Closed-Ended**

"Do video games affect mood?"

Can be answered with just "yes" or "no"&mdash;limited exploration.

- Easy to quantify and analyze
- Good for specific, categorizable information such as "Do you have a library card?"
- Useful for gathering straightforward facts or opinions you can count
]
]]

.pull-right[.font90[
.content-box-green[
**Open-Ended**

"How might playing video games affect the mood of middle school students?"

Invites exploration of different effects, game types, and conditions.

- Require detailed, free-form responses
- Provide rich, nuanced information
- Harder to analyze quickly
]
]]

---
### .font70[BRIC-FO.red[R]:] Researchable Questions

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-yellow[
**Not Easily Researchable**

"Is there life on other planets?"

Fascinating but beyond a student's ability to gather original data.
]

.content-box-green[
**Researchable Version**

"What do high school students believe about life on other planets?"

Can be investigated through surveys and interviews.
]

.content-box-blue[
**Key Consideration**

Can you gather information to answer this using available tools?
]
]]

.pull-right[
```{r img8, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="72%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/08-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

---
### Using the 5 W's (and How)

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("user", height = "2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Who**

Who is involved or affected? (teenagers, athletes, teachers, polar bears)
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**What**

What aspect interests you? (mental health, economic cost, performance)
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("location-dot", height = "2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Where**

A certain location or context? (your city, online communities, lakes)
]
]

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("clock", height = "2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**When**

A time period? (past 5 years, during summer, historical period)
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("gears", height = "2em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Why/How**

Causes or processes? (why something happens, how factors interact)
]
]

---
### Example: Narrowing "Video Games"

<br>

.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("gamepad", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Broad Topic**

Video games (huge topic with many aspects)
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("brain", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Narrower Focus**

Video games and learning (educational aspect)
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("puzzle-piece", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Specific Angle**

Video games and problem-solving skills
]

### From Topic to Research Question

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-blue[
**Broad Topic**

Video games
]

.content-box-blue[
**Research Question**

"Can playing video games improve middle school students' problem-solving skills, and if so, how?"
]
]]

.pull-right[.font90[
.content-box-blue[
**Narrower Focus**

Video games and problem-solving skills
]

.content-box-green[
**Elements**

- **Who:** middle school students
- **What:** effect on problem-solving skills
- **Open-ended:** asks "how" not just "if"
]
]]

> "The formulation of a problem is often more essential than its solution, which may be merely a matter of mathematical or experimental skill.” ~ Albert Einstein

`r fontawesome::fa("gears", height = "1.6em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**Why/How**

Causes or processes? (why something happens, how factors interact)
]
]
]

---
### Peer Review Carousel `r fontawesome::fa("rotate", fill = "#A4123F")`

#### <span style="color:#A4123F;">Put your draft questions to the test with the BRIC-FOR criteria!</span>

.pull-left[.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Post your drafts</strong><br>
  Each team posts their draft research questions on the whiteboard.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Rotate & review</strong><br>
  Teams rotate around the room and leave post-it feedback using the <strong>BRIC-FOR</strong> criteria. <em>(10 min)</em></div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Debrief</strong><br>
  Return to your questions, read the feedback, and discuss as a class. <em>(10 min)</em></div>
</div>
]]

.pull-right[.font80[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("clipboard-check", fill = "#4a7fb5")` BRIC-FOR Checklist**

- **B**alanced (Well-Scoped)
- **R**elevant & **I**nteresting
- **C**lear & **F**ocused
- **O**pen-ended
- **R**esearchable
]
]]

---
### From Questions to Hypotheses

<br>

.font120[The information you have collected from the literature may help you translate your questions to **hypotheses**.]

--

<br>

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**Singular:** Hypothesis
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**Plural:** Hypotheses
]
]

---
### What is a Hypothesis?

<br>
<br>

.content-box-blue[
**An educated guess** about what you expect to find based on your research question.
]

--

<br>
<br>

#### `r fontawesome::fa("book-open-reader", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Good hypotheses are developed from prior knowledge, preliminary research, and logical reasoning.

--

<br>
<br>

#### `r fontawesome::fa("flask-vial", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; A hypothesis transforms your curiosity into a **testable prediction** that guides your research process.


---
background-image: url("assets/07-strip.png")
background-position: 5% 10%
background-size: 100% 20%
class: center, middle

<br>

<br>

<br>

### Characteristics of a Good Hypothesis

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**It's a statement, not a question**

Directly answers your research question or predicts an outcome.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("vial-circle-check", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**It is testable**

You can gather data to support or refute it.
]
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("diagram-project", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**It predicts a relationship between variables**

Often phrased as "If X happens, then Y will happen."
]
]

---
background-image: url("assets/07-strip.png")
background-position: 5% 10%
background-size: 100% 20%
class: center, middle

<br>

<br>

<br>

### Characteristics of a Good Hypothesis

.three-col[
.col[
`r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", height = "2.5em", fill = "#4a7fb5")`

**There is a structure for the way we make a prediction:
**

]
.col[
 '.red[We hypothesize that [IV] is [positively/negatively/not] associated with [DV] among [population], because [brief rationale].]'

]
]

---
### Example: Study Time Hypothesis

.pull-left[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Question**

"How does the amount of time spent studying affect test scores among 8th graders?"
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Hypothesis**

"8th graders who study for at least 2 hours a day will have higher test scores than those who study for less than 1 hour a day."
]
]

--

.pull-right[.font90[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It's a statement
Predicting an outcome (more study &rarr; higher scores).

#### `r fontawesome::fa("vial-circle-check", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It's testable
You could gather data on study habits and test scores.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("people-group", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It mentions specific groups to compare
Those who study &ge;2 hours vs. those who study &lt;1 hour.
]]

---
### Example: Sleep and Sugary Drinks

.pull-left[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Research Question**

"Does drinking sugary drinks before bed affect sleep quality in teenagers?"
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Hypothesis**

"Drinking sugary drinks in the evening will lead to poorer sleep quality in teenagers, with more frequent waking during the night."
]
]

--

.pull-right[.font90[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It's a statement

#### `r fontawesome::fa("vial-circle-check", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It's testable
Through comparison of sleep patterns.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("people-group", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It mentions a specific group

#### `r fontawesome::fa("arrow-right", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; It predicts an effect (poorer sleep) and gives a rationale (sugar disrupts sleep)
]]

---
### Variables in Research

.pull-left[
```{r img8a, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/08-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font90[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("sliders", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Independent Variable**

What you change or what differs between groups. The potential cause or input you're testing. *Example: amount of study time.*
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("gauge-high", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Dependent Variable**

What you measure as the outcome. The effect that might change based on the independent variable. *Example: test scores.*
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("equals", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Hypothesis Formula**

"If [independent variable], then [dependent variable], because [reason]."
]
]]

---
### Your Turn: Formulate a Hypothesis

.pull-left[
```{r img9, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/09-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Make a Prediction</strong><br>
  Based on what you know, what do you expect to find?</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Write as a Statement</strong><br>
  Not a question &mdash; a clear prediction of what will happen.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Identify &amp; Include Variables</strong><br>
  Connect your independent and dependent variables.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">4</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Add Reasoning</strong><br>
  Explain why you expect this outcome ("because...").</div>
</div>
]]

### Scientific Storytelling: Variable Sentence Practice

#### <span style="color:#A4123F;">Turn your variables into one clear, testable prediction.</span>

.center[.font120[.content-box-blue[
"We predict that **[IV]** is associated with **[DV]** because **[rationale based on prior knowledge]**."
]]]

.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev-sm">`r fontawesome::fa("pen-nib", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Write</strong> &mdash; As a team, write <strong>one sentence</strong> in the format above.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev-sm">`r fontawesome::fa("bullhorn", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>

</div>

<div class="chev-row">

</div>
